Following Labour's victory in the 1997 general election, its largest landslide general election victory in history, Prime Minister Tony Blair appointed Gordon Brown as Chancellor of the Exchequer.

The CRUT must distribute a fixed percentage annuity to the non-charitable beneficiary.
This percentage may not be less than 5 percent nor more than 50 percent of the net fair market value of the CRUT's assets.
As may be seen, the amount of the annuity might vary from year to year, but the percentage always stays the same.
For example, assume a 10% CRUT is established, and assume the value of its portfolio holdings in year 1 is $1 million.
The annuity that year is $100,000.
Assuming the portfolio drops in value, and in year 2 is worth $900,000.
No other payments
The CRUT may not distribute any of its assets to anyone other than the annuity recipient or the qualified charity beneficiary.

The CRUT may not let any of its assets be used for the benefit of anyone other than the annuity recipient, the qualified charitable beneficiary, or a charitable organization as described in section 170.

Once the annuity period is over, the remainder of the CRUT principal is distributed to charity.

The annuity percentage, multiplied by the fair market value of the CRUT's assets; or 2.

Assume the CRUT has only $70,000 of income that year.

In its first year of trading, Chelmsford Star Industrial Co-operative Society had a membership of 275 and annual sales of £4,316.
By 1900, with 1,439 registered co-operatives in the UK, membership had risen to 2,001, with annual sales of £40,414.
In 1954, with membership standing at 19,089, the Society achieved sales of over £1 million for the first time.
Activities

As of May 2019, the Society operates 40 convenience stores under The Co-operative Food fascia, 2 Quadrant department stores in Chelmsford and Braintree, and eight Chelmsford Star Co-operative Funeral Services.
Food retailing provides the lion's share of the Society's operating profits, while its two Quadrant department stores made a 2018-19 operating loss.
Membership of the society is open to all residents of the Society's mid-Essex trading area, with members receiving a share of the profits in the form of dividend.
The Co-op convenience store on New Street in central Chelmsford belongs to the national Co-operative Group, and not to the Chelmsford Star Society.

History
Nabisco continued to expand the facilities until the company's departure for the suburbs in 1958.
The final configuration consists of 19 separate structures taking up the entire city block, and included both production areas and offices.
The building on the Tenth Avenue side is a later structure designed in the 1930s by Nabisco's then-architect Louis Wirsching Jr. that replaced the original baking facilities there.
Rail and aluminum-clad walking bridge connections were also added going across 10th Avenue to tie in the existing 85 Tenth Avenue building across the street.
